Implement the user's final Korvo demo integration: the existing native openvela factory_demo is the main interface, with an interactive button to enter digit recognition and a Return control that restores the main dashboard. One firmware, no reflashing to switch views. Root is handling Function Ethernet hardware separately. You own only private candidate files/reports/builds under /mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/factory-digit-integration-e407; never edit maintained source or accepted build outputs. Do not touch serial, boards, USBIP, Windows host networking, AI logs or publication. Do not spawn additional workers.
Reuse native factory code at openvela-dev/frameworks/runtimes/services/xmsdemo/factory (FactoryActivity, FactoryBackend, FactoryLifecycle, Dashboard, native AM/PM/WM). Existing backend delivers immutable RGB565 240x240 CameraFrame leases; no second camera opener, no frame ownership races, no inference blocking the LVGL thread. The accepted factory profile is korvo-openvela-factory, FLAT single-core because USB/SD/ADC profiles have guards. Do not enable SMP or bypass guards just to integrate views. Preserve the independent stable dual-core/PIE demo and its evidence; a same-image integration must state its actual execution mode and measured behavior, never reuse the old FPS as a new result.
Reuse the actual stable digit model and preprocessing/inference from /home/regex/work/esp32s31-vision-demo/openvela-dev/apps/examples/s31digit (digit_infer.h, digit_model.h, s31digit_main.c, s31digit_ops.S), also inspect the current main engineering tree's corresponding source and tools/s31-digit/README.md for origin/licensing. The stable package's source/model identity review is under backups/factory-demo-port/digit-delivery-worker. Preserve model bytes and recognition semantics. Prefer native portable inference for the integrated single-core profile if the exact SIMD routine cannot safely be reused; document that clearly. No invented recognition output or confidence/FPS. An actual camera frame must produce each displayed inference result. Display the chosen crop and processed input where practical. Maintain bounded owned worker/frame storage; entering/exiting/re-entering and Activity pause/destroy must drain work without touching destroyed LVGL objects. Retain existing camera preview/coffee/audio/storage behavior.
Deliver source overlays under files/<workspace-relative-path>, an integration patch, changed-file/base hashes, host checks using real model/preprocess samples and lifecycle transitions, and a concise readiness report. Add minimal AM action hooks (e.g. s31.factory.digit/dashboard/snapshot) for Root's serial-driven validation while using the exact same UI path as touch. Investigate how the final factory profile can be made the default HOME/main interface using native lifecycle, but do not alter unrelated profiles; if not safe to bundle, report an exact separate patch proposal. Root will test real screen interaction. Build your private candidate if existing helpers can be reused safely, using only a fresh output. Start by inspecting the existing factory build scripts and new output options; do not overwrite build-v1 or the source-export receiver. No dependency upgrades/downloads. Retain original third-party license notices.
Report promptly if a concrete blocker prevents this workflow; otherwise complete the candidate and checks, with clear untested board boundaries. Use focused reads and avoid recursive traversal of huge build/history trees.

I’ll first inspect the factory build helpers and their fresh-output options, then read the native factory lifecycle and stable digit implementation. All changes and build artifacts will stay in the private delivery directory; board interaction remains for Root.

The factory helper supports a fresh output and source overlays, so it can be adapted without touching `build-v1`. The stable digit header provides the original scalar inference path. I’m tracing its camera preprocessing next so the integrated view preserves the live recognition behavior as well as the model bytes.

The live camera demo adds Otsu segmentation and a consecutive-frame acceptance rule around the shared digit model. I’ll preserve those rules and use a centered 200×200 crop from the factory’s 240×240 frame. Inference will run on the existing lifecycle worker with one owned work slot; Return and pause will invalidate pending results without waiting on the UI thread.

The candidate now has the dashboard button, a digit view with the analyzed crop and processed input, and Return navigation through the same deferred path as the AM hooks. I also found a profile-scoped HOME solution: generate ROMFS manifests that assign HOME to FactoryActivity only when the factory option is enabled. Next are host lifecycle checks and a fresh firmware build.

The model checks pass: all 100 bundled MNIST inputs retain their predictions, and 400 RGB565 fixture frames match the original preprocessing and acceptance rules. Blank, low-ink, and overfilled crops are rejected. These are host fixtures, not camera measurements. The real-LVGL lifecycle test is now exercising navigation and pause/destroy during inference.

The LVGL lifecycle checks pass under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, including Return/re-entry, pause/resume, destroy during inference, stale-result expiry, and backend reuse. Render review caught an overlapping caption; I fixed it and reran the checks. Firmware compilation is underway with FLAT and single-core settings intact.

The HOME-generation check passes: enabling it changes only the generated factory and launcher action filters; disabling it leaves both manifests byte-identical to their originals. The integration patch also replays cleanly against the recorded base files. One board-test detail is documented: the factory’s 200×200 preview crop covers a larger sensor area than the independent VGA demo’s crop.

The private build has reached the native service and UI libraries with no compiler errors reported so far. The handoff now includes the AM commands, result-freshness fields, and the board checks still needed. Final validation will check the linked image for the unchanged model constants and the absence of the PIE dot routine.

The source overlay and patch are finalized, and their maintained base hashes still match. The build is finishing its remaining libraries. The delivery will stay marked as a candidate until Root verifies cold boot, real touch navigation, camera recognition, and target timing.

All 13 preservation hashes for the independent stable demo still match its original receipt. The private build is compiling the final service/application sources; the host checks and patch replay are complete.

Final review found that a long camera error could overlap the new button. I bounded the status text above it and am rerunning the UI check. This small fix will be included in the final private relink.

The final UI check passes. I also retained the existing AM action-completion acknowledgements so Root’s serial validation can keep using them; they are emitted after the shared touch/AM transition completes.

The latest UI/lifecycle run passes, including the retained AM completion acknowledgements. The firmware build is waiting on its existing multimedia dependency. I’ll let that finish, then link and validate the final image.

The generated ROMFS has exactly one HOME resolver: `FactoryActivity`. The launcher’s HOME action is absent from this candidate’s ROMFS, which confirms the packaging change reached the filesystem image. The multimedia dependency step is still progressing.

The source and host checks are complete. FFmpeg’s dependency scan is the remaining slow step; its output continues to grow, so the build is progressing. I’m keeping the private build running through the final link.

FFmpeg has generated 246 dependency entries; the existing factory build has 281. There are still no reported build errors. The remaining verification is the firmware link and the final image’s constants, symbols, and flash bounds.
The dependency scan is near completion at 274 entries. No blocker has appeared; I’m waiting for the remaining library build and final firmware checks.
FFmpeg’s dependency scan has completed and compilation has started. The slow step has cleared; the remaining work is library compilation, the final link, and image verification.
Multimedia compilation is progressing without reported errors. The overlay and host checks are complete; I’m waiting for the firmware build so the handoff can include a verified image hash.
FFmpeg is compiling its final sources. The factory application objects and firmware link should follow next. Nothing has been flashed or changed outside the private candidate area.
All 281 FFmpeg object files have been created. Its archive step is still running before the factory targets can finish. The integration checks remain passing.

The new digit worker, digit view, Activity integration, and lifecycle code have compiled successfully for the target. The build is now linking the firmware; next I’ll apply the final UI refinements within this private output and verify the resulting image.

The firmware linked successfully, but the provenance check found that a compile input changed during the build. The protected source configuration files are unchanged. I’m identifying the changed input before accepting the candidate’s build record.

The changed input is a generated JIDL file inside the private build directory. CMake creates it empty at configuration time, then generates its contents before compilation. No maintained source changed. I’m correcting the build record to track generated outputs separately, then completing the final relink.

The provenance review is resolved: the only change was the private JIDL output, and all immutable source hashes still match. The final private rebuild is running now. The original build record and first image are preserved alongside it.

I found a build timestamp issue: copying the final edits preserved source timestamps older than the existing object files, so Ninja skipped those edits. I’ve invalidated the three affected private objects. The next check will require their recompilation and verify the final UI strings in the linked image.

The final firmware build and image checks pass. The image contains the unchanged model constants and the HOME ROMFS, includes the final UI edits, and has no SIMD dot routine. It fits below the persistent-data region. I’m recording the final hashes and handoff paths now.

Implemented and built the private candidate: factory HOME → digit recognition → Return, in one FLAT, single-core firmware using the original scalar model.
